widgets_values:
CUPID3D ON A CLEANED PLATE

Reconstructs the subject in 3D and drops it back onto the same photo with the subject painted out, so it can be moved around the scene freely.

NEEDS, BEYOND THIS PACK
- ComfyUI-NKD-Klein-Tools — Klein Pre/Postsampling, Box Detections
- ComfyUI-NKD-Basic-Tools — NKD Loader
- ComfyUI-NKD-VFX-Tools — NKD Preview 3D
- RES4LYF — ClownsharKSampler Beta
- basic_data_handling — IfElse
Models: birefnet.safetensors for Remove Background, and the "Klein 3 Distilled" bundle inside NKD Loader.

THE FLOW
- Remove Background (BiRefNet) returns a FOREGROUND mask, so it feeds Cupid3D straight in. No InvertMask here — that is only needed for LoadImage's own MASK, which is 1 - alpha.
- The Klein 3 pass reuses that same mask as a "remove" edit: it paints the subject out of the photo and leaves a clean plate.
- IfElse picks what the viewer sits on — the cleaned plate (true) or the untouched photo (false). Whatever it picks also sets the render size through Get Image Size, so the camera and the plate can never disagree.
- camera_info describes the input image exactly as it was fed in, so the plate needs no reframing.

place_on_ground puts the mesh on y=0, resting on the viewer's floor rather than straddling the origin; the camera moves with it. crop_to_content is off in this one, so the pose is solved on the full frame.

Swap the photo for your own and the only thing to revisit is the Klein prompt and the box detections.

widgets_values_named.text:
CUPID3D — one image in, a 3D mesh plus the camera that shot it.

First run downloads ~7 GB of weights from hbb1/Cupid, then takes a minute or so. Peak VRAM is about 11.5 GB.

WHY THE EXTRA NODES

- InvertMask: LoadImage's MASK is 1 - alpha, so it marks the background. Cupid3D wants the subject. Segmentation nodes (RMBG, SAM) already give the subject, so they wire straight in with no InvertMask. With no mask at all, rembg removes the background itself.

- GetImageSize -> RenderMesh width/height: Cupid predicts an off-centre principal point, and LOAD3D_CAMERA has no field for one, so the node pads the frame until that point is centred. 'camera_frame' is that padded frame, and it is what the camera describes. Render at its size and composite against it, not against the original image.

camera_info is a plain LOAD3D_CAMERA, so it also drives Preview3D, Load3D and the NKD VFX Tools camera nodes.

The mesh carries vertex colours, not a baked texture. For UVs and a texture, run it through UnwrapMesh and BakeTextureFromViews.
